claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: 22.9 km actual less 21.3 km recommended is 1.60 km, which is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance but under POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling. This is therefore not a within-tolerance case, so the no-refund tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 cannot apply, and the distance limb of POL-RD-25 does not send this case to a human reviewer.

The driver-device trace fixes exactly when the vehicle left the recommended alignment - the fixes run on the Pan-Island Expressway until 08:11:37, switch to Dunearn Road at 08:12:07 and stay on Dunearn Road and Bukit Timah Road until the rejoin at 08:22:49 - which is the 'point of deviation' that POL-RD-21 requires the driver's in-app notice to precede or coincide with, and it shows the rider spent roughly ten minutes off the recommended route while the meter ran.

The only notice the driver relies on is MSG-05011-003, and the artifact carrying it is impaired: EV-CHAT-05011 has weight_multiplier 0.4 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT (severity HIGH), and the conflict falls exactly across the deviation event - the driver-device clock puts that message at 08:10:49, before the deviation, and the server clock puts its delivery at 08:14:19, after it. Because the pre-deviation notice rests on this impaired and irreconcilable entry, POL-RD-21's requirement that the rider be informed before or at the point of deviation is not established, and the driver cannot bring the case within POL-RD-24(a), the one row that returns no refund to the rider.

The rider's 'ok can' at 08:14:39 cannot supply the agreement that row (a) of POL-RD-24 needs: it was sent after the vehicle had already left the recommended route at 08:12:19, so it is a reaction to a deviation already under way, not consent to a reroute proposed and taken before the turn. The artifact carrying it, EV-CHAT-05011, is impaired at weight 0.4 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT), so it cannot be read as the rider's agreement at any confidence above 0.4.

With the deviation at 1.60 km and no notice shown before or at the point of deviation, the rider recovers the excess distance fare under POL-RD-24: row (b) if the PIE accident advisory justifies the reroute and row (d) if it does not - both rows return that fare, so the rider's position is the same whichever way the traffic element is decided. On the fare breakdown that is 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.15 SGD, at the base per-km rate and without surge, and the rider currently carries it because payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The matrix measures this remedy by the excess distance fare and not by the whole fare, so 1.15 SGD, not the 37.55 SGD the rider asks for, is the sum this case can move under POL-RD-24.

If the judge finds the notice fact genuinely unestablished rather than established as late, then the open question is one POL-GEN-26 names in terms - whether the driver notified the rider - and the only artifact that would answer it is impaired at 0.4, so under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence on the deciding fact cannot pass 0.4 and falls below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 requires on a 37.55 SGD dispute. The same is true of whether the accident advisory intersects the recommended route, which the package itself leaves undetermined for the judge. On that reading the case escalates and the 37.55 SGD is held rather than collected, which leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge while a human reviews it; the rider's alternative to the 1.15 SGD refund above is escalation, not NO_ACTION.

claims.text: The reroute is traffic-justified on the platform's own traffic data, which is all POL-RD-23 asks for. EV-ADVIS-05011-01 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) is an LTA traffic-incident advisory of type ACCIDENT — a type POL-RD-23 admits as an incident — on the Pan-Island Expressway, direction towards Changi, location 'after Adam Road exit', valid 07:44:37 to 08:54:37. That window covers both the deviation (logged 08:12:19) and the rejoin (08:22:49). The recommended route itself runs on the PIE — trip_record.optimal_route_via is 'Choa Chu Kang Avenue 4, Kranji Expressway (KJE), Pan-Island Expressway (PIE), Central Expressway (CTE), Outram Road' — and the platform's own deviation event records that the vehicle left the recommended route at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit, i.e. on that same PIE leg of the recommended route, while the advisory was live. Same expressway, matching direction of travel on that leg, overlapping window: the advisory intersects the recommended route and the driver's reroute was a response to a real incident, not a preference.

The driver informed the rider by in-app chat before the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. MSG-05011-003 — 'Accident on PIE after Adam Rd, I exit Eng Neo and go Bukit Timah ok?' — carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49, ninety seconds before the platform logged route_deviation_detected at 08:12:19, and its read receipt is 08:11:13, also before the deviation. The rider answered 'ok can' (MSG-05011-004), so the deviation is agreed on the chat log's face. I disclose that EV-CHAT-05011 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: the single delivered_at value for MSG-05011-003 (08:14:19) disagrees with that same entry's sent_at and cannot be reconciled with its own read_at of 08:11:13 — a message cannot be read before it is delivered — so the outlier is one server-side delivery stamp, not the message, its contents, or the rider's acknowledgment, all of which the impaired log still carries. The rider's assertion that the driver 'did not ask me before turning' is contradicted by her own reply on the record.

The deviation is measured the way POL-RD-22 prescribes, from the platform's recorded distances: actual 22.9 km less optimal 21.3 km = 1.60 km. That is above the 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22) and therefore outside it, and it is at or below the 2.0 km ceiling POL-RD-25 puts on an AI ruling on a route deviation — 1.60 km, not the 4.3 km of DISP-001 that must be escalated. The dispute value is 37.55 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's 10.00-50.00 SGD band where an AI ruling stands at 0.80 confidence, and neither profile carries a fraud flag of 1 or more, so the 0.95 band does not apply. This case is one the AI can and should decide, not refer.

The case therefore falls on row (a) of POL-RD-24 — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — and row (a) returns no refund, with the result that the rider's claim to the whole 37.55 SGD fare is not supported and the present state stands under POL-GEN-03. The driver turned off a route carrying a live accident advisory, told the rider by chat before he exited, gave a brief reason, and the rider answered 'ok can'. The element of informed, agreed travel that row (a) turns on is carried by EV-CHAT-05011, which is impaired at weight 0.4 on issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, as set out above.

Even on the rows of POL-RD-24 that favour the rider, the remedy is the excess distance fare only, and only at the base per-km rate without surge: 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.15 SGD. No row of the matrix returns the trip fare, so the rider's demand for the full 37.55 SGD fails on the policy's own arithmetic whatever the judge finds on justification or notification. The fare itself is correctly built on the metered ledger — base 2.80, distance 16.49, time 6.21, ERP 3.50, platform fee 0.90, surge 7.65 — and nothing in the itemisation is disputed as an arithmetic error.

The GPS trace cannot be used to shrink the deviation. EV-GPS-05011 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) measures 19.158 km over 70 fixes — shorter than either recorded distance — and POL-RD-22 says in terms that the trace shows which route was taken and when and is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The trace the rider may point to therefore proves only the route taken (PIE to Eng Neo, Dunearn Road, Bukit Timah Road, rejoin at the CTE slip road), which the trip record already states; the deviation remains 1.60 km.

If the judge finds the notification limb cannot be established at all on an artifact impaired to weight 0.4 — so that the case fits neither row (a) nor row (b) of POL-RD-24 — the consequence is escalation under POL-GEN-26, not a refund: the open question is stated and the fare is held while a human reviews it, because ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and replaces any ruling (POL-GEN-03). An escalated fare is not a returned fare, and on this record there is no basis for any order that returns the trip fare to the rider.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This dispute cannot be decided on this record, so it goes to a human reviewer, and the disputed 37.55 SGD is held — not collected from the rider and not refunded to her — until that review.

1. Distance is settled. The platform's recorded distances are 22.9 km actual against 21.3 km recommended, so the deviation is 1.60 km (EV-TRIP-05011; POL-RD-22, v2.1 1.4). That is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 do not apply, and it is at or below the 2.0 km ceiling POL-RD-25 sets for an AI ruling (v2.1 6.2), so distance alone does not force escalation. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05011) measures 19.158 km, but POL-RD-22 says the trace is not used to re-measure distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length; it shows only which route was taken, which the trip record already states.

2. The reroute is traffic-justified. EV-ADVIS-05011-01 is a live LTA accident advisory on the PIE towards Changi after the Adam Road exit, valid 07:44:37–08:54:37. The recommended route runs on the PIE, the vehicle was on that leg until it left at the PIE / Eng Neo Avenue exit at 08:12:19, and the advisory's window covers both the deviation and the rejoin at 08:22:49. It intersects the recommended route in the direction of travel, so POL-RD-23 is satisfied.

3. Notification is the fact the record cannot establish. Which row of POL-RD-24 applies now turns on POL-RD-21: whether the driver informed the rider of the deviation by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and whether the rider agreed. Everything on that question rests on one entry, MSG-05011-003, in EV-CHAT-05011, and that artifact is impaired: weight_multiplier 0.4, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT (severity HIGH). The driver's device clock puts the message at 08:10:49, ninety seconds before the platform logged the deviation at 08:12:19; the server clock puts its delivery at 08:14:19, nearly two minutes after; and the entry's own read receipt (08:11:13) precedes its delivery stamp, so the log contradicts itself on exactly the moment the rule turns on. The rider's reply 'ok can' (08:14:39) is after the deviation had begun on either clock. I can therefore find neither that the driver informed the rider before or at the point of deviation, nor that he did not: the limb is undecided.

4. Consequence. The case fits neither POL-RD-24(a) (traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed — no refund) nor POL-RD-24(b) (traffic-justified, rider not informed — refund of the excess distance fare), and POL-RD-24 sends a case that fits no row to POL-GEN-26; POL-GEN-26 names 'whether the driver notified the rider' as a fact that is escalated, not decided, when the evidence carrying it is impaired. Independently, POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the weight of the artifact carrying the deciding fact — 0.4 here — while POL-GEN-22 and POL-RD-25 require 0.80 on a 37.55 SGD route deviation (value band 10.00–50.00 SGD, no fraud flag, deviation under 2.0 km). 0.4 is below that bar. On both grounds the ruling is ESCALATE.

5. On the claims. The driver's claim that MSG-05011-003 proves notice before the deviation is not accepted beyond 0.4, because the artifact is impaired precisely on that timing; the rest of the driver's case (distance arithmetic, no row returning the whole fare, the trace not shrinking the deviation) stands. The rider's claim that the pre-deviation notice is not established is accepted as far as it goes, but the limb is undecided rather than negatived, so it yields no refund on its own; the rider's alternative claim for the excess distance fare — 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD, at the base per-km rate without surge — is the arithmetic POL-RD-24 uses and I do not disturb it, but no row can be selected on this record, so it does not issue now; and the rider's demand for the full 37.55 SGD has no support in any row of the matrix, whose maximum is 1.15 SGD.

Open question for the human reviewer: whether the driver's reroute message was in fact sent and read before the vehicle left the PIE at 08:12:19. Reconciling the driver-device clock and the server delivery stamp for MSG-05011-003, together with the rider's read receipt, should settle which row of POL-RD-24 applies.

To both parties: this case goes to a human reviewer, and the 37.55 SGD in dispute is held — not collected from the rider and not refunded to her — until that review. Here is why.

What is settled. The trip did leave the recommended route. On the platform's recorded distances (POL-RD-22): 22.9 km actual minus 21.3 km recommended = 1.60 km of deviation. That is over the 1.0 km tolerance but under the 2.0 km ceiling in POL-RD-25, so the distance alone does not send this to a human. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05011-01 (weight 1.0) is a real ACCIDENT on the PIE towards Changi after the Adam Road exit, live 07:44–08:54 and so overlapping the trip; that is the PIE leg of the recommended route, in the direction of travel, at the very point where the driver left it — so the reroute is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The GPS trace EV-GPS-05011 (weight 1.0) shows which route was taken and when, and per POL-RD-22 is not used to re-measure the distance, so it cannot shrink the 1.60 km.

What cannot be settled, and decides the case. POL-RD-24 turns on whether the driver informed the rider before or at the point of deviation (POL-RD-21). Row (a) — no refund — needs the rider informed and agreeing; row (b) — refund of the excess distance fare — needs her not informed. That fact rests on one artifact, the in-app chat EV-CHAT-05011, which the pre-pass marks IMPAIRED, weight 0.4, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT: the driver's reroute message MSG-05011-003 carries a driver-device sent_at of 08:10:49 (before the 08:12:19 deviation) and a server delivered_at of 08:14:19 (after it), and the entry's own read receipt of 08:11:13 cannot precede its delivery. The two clocks straddle the deviation and nothing in the record says which is right, so it cannot be established whether the notice came before the turn or after it. The rider's 'ok can' reply sits in the same impaired log. The driver's own account in the dispute is a bare assertion, and POL-RD-21 says a notice not backed by the chat log or a call recording cannot be established. An undecided limb supports neither the no-refund row nor the refund row, so no row of POL-RD-24 fits; POL-RD-24 and POL-GEN-26 both send such a case to a human reviewer.

Money. The most any row of the matrix could return is the excess distance fare, 1.60 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.15 SGD (rows (b)/(d)); row (a) would return nothing; and no row returns the whole 37.55 SGD fare the rider asks for (metered total 37.55 = base 2.80 + distance 16.49 + time 6.21 + ERP 3.50 + platform fee 0.90, plus surge 7.65). None of those amounts is ordered today.

Confidence. The pivotal fact is carried only by the 0.4 chat log, so confidence is capped at 0.40 (POL-GEN-02(2)), below the 0.80 that POL-GEN-22 and POL-RD-25 require on a 37.55 SGD route deviation. Neither profile carries a fraud flag, so 0.80 and not 0.95 is the bar. No route-deviation clause in this version produces a referral.

So the rider's fall-back rows are cut down: POL-RD-24(d) (not traffic-justified) does not arise, and in any event no row of POL-RD-24 returns the whole fare — the most it ever returns is the excess distance fare, 1.60 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.15 SGD, not the 37.55 SGD claimed.

What cannot be settled, and the reason for the referral. The traffic limb is settled above and need not be reopened.

The dispute value is 37.55 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's 10.00-50.00 SGD band where an AI ruling stands at 0.80 confidence, and neither profile carries a fraud flag of 1 or more, so the 0.95 band does not apply. This case is one the AI can and should decide, not refer.

The case therefore falls on row (a) of POL-RD-24 — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — and row (a) returns no refund, with the result that the rider's claim to the whole 37.55 SGD fare is not supported and the present state stands under POL-GEN-03. The driver turned off a route carrying a live accident advisory, told the rider by chat before he exited, gave a brief reason, and the rider answered 'ok can'. The element of informed, agreed travel that row (a) turns on is carried by EV-CHAT-05011, which is impaired at weight 0.4 on issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, as set out above.

Even on the rows of POL-RD-24 that favour the rider, the remedy is the excess distance fare only, and only at the base per-km rate without surge: 1.60 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.15 SGD. No row of the matrix returns the trip fare, so the rider's demand for the full 37.55 SGD fails on the policy's own arithmetic whatever the judge finds on justification or notification. The fare itself is correctly built on the metered ledger — base 2.80, distance 16.49, time 6.21, ERP 3.50, platform fee 0.90, surge 7.65 — and nothing in the itemisation is disputed as an arithmetic error.

The GPS trace cannot be used to shrink the deviation. EV-GPS-05011 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) measures 19.158 km over 70 fixes — shorter than either recorded distance — and POL-RD-22 says in terms that the trace shows which route was taken and when and is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length. The trace the rider may point to therefore proves only the route taken (PIE to Eng Neo, Dunearn Road, Bukit Timah Road, rejoin at the CTE slip road), which the trip record already states; the deviation remains 1.60 km.

If the judge finds the notification limb cannot be established at all on an artifact impaired to weight 0.4 — so that the case fits neither row (a) nor row (b) of POL-RD-24 — the consequence is escalation under POL-GEN-26, not a refund: the open question is stated and the fare is held while a human reviews it, because ESCALATE issues no monetary outcome and replaces any ruling (POL-GEN-03). An escalated fare is not a returned fare, and on this record there is no basis for any order that returns the trip fare to the rider.
